slice: 0.8.7 X7b: the exam's blockers (six, as the coordinator decided)
summary: All six X7 blockers are fixed. (1) READ's desk list is now primed together with READ's brief (brain_briefs.open_desk, keyed by the sha256 of messages 1 to 3, so a changed desk re-primes). This happens at Ready for the owner's desk (after_start, through brain_briefs.DESKS) and before any READ question whose messages 1 to 3 the worker does not keep (understand.keep_desk, called by understand.ask and by the exam). Home Demo's first READ now reads 42 new tokens instead of 299 and is sent. READ's cap stays at 250; the 400-token fallback was not needed. (2) A MARKS item is right when every kept mark is in the known set and at least one is found, with precision and recall recorded per item and per paper. (3) Asking is not harm: wrong_used and the READ markers now count only TAKEN or TRIMMED answers. (4) NEXT items go through judgment.ask_next (NEXT, then ORDER when due, with the tripwire), the final outcome is marked, and the first and reversed picks are kept on the row. (5) brief.vocabulary reads the Qwen3.5 4B GGUF. (6) tests_integrated/data/exam/DISAGREEMENTS.md lists the disagreements. The papers are unchanged. The READ.asks marker also gained a small fix: it now reads a question option's title as its handle. No real model was loaded.

files_changed.workbench/brain_briefs.py: X7b. prime(port, kind, held=None) can prime messages 1 to 3 (brief, desk, 'Ready.') plus PRIME_LINE and record them as the kind's last prefix, with desk = a 16-hex digest. New: DESKS registry, desk_kept, open_desk(port, kind, messages, request=None), which returns KEPT, PRIMED or NOT_PRIMED. With a request, open_desk skips the prime if the request is stopped or has less than 3 s left, and charges the time it spends to the request's ceiling. open_desks(kernel, port) runs at after_start. summary() lists desks. The docstring is updated: the desk, and Forget re-priming the desk as it stands.
files_changed.workbench/understand.py: X7b block. keep_desk(i, request) primes READ's messages 1 to 3 unless they are kept. It is called in ask(), so it covers her hand and requests.read. desk_layout(kernel) gives the owner's desk at Ready and is registered as DESKS['READ']. exam_ask(i, request, item) is the exam's READ path.

existing_tests_changed: None. No test was run (the owner's rule).
decisions: (1) I primed rather than raising the cap. The priming read is the A2 mechanism with messages 1 to 3 in place of the brief alone, and it is keyed by their sha256. It runs at Ready (open_desks) and inline before a READ question when the desk is not kept, because the exam's desks and a changed desk are only known at question time. It is not a turn: nothing is recorded. Its time is charged to the request's ceiling, it is skipped when the request is stopped or has less than 3 s left, and READ's caps are unchanged.

desk_layout reads the owner's desk at Ready using the selection's owner (a read principal) and reading.lexicon. It never raises; if it fails, the first question primes the desk instead. This path was not exercised on a Kernel in the smoke, only through a stub provider.

(4) I routed every NEXT item through ask_next, not only STEER's, because that is the program's one path. CHOOSE results are unchanged: those items have no page, so ORDER is never due. An OFFER, a planted change shown as a card, still counts as the model's pick, as the paper's rule says ('passes every check').

I also fixed the READ.asks marker so it reads an option's title as its handle on the exam desk. This made read-ambiguous-02 right. It is a runner defect in the same scoring family and was not one of the six.
(3) TRIMMED counts as taken, the same as TAKEN.
not_done: No new tests. The suite, tiers and window checks were not run. Nothing was tested in the owner's sense, and nothing ran on the ThinkPad. No model was loaded; only the 4B header was read, for its vocabulary.

Not fixed, only reported in DISAGREEMENTS.md and here: MARKS CEILING_TIME on the 4B; the order test cannot catch a pick of the middle of three options; the doorway does not flag steer-16's 'Assistant:' lines; the READ naming issues (CURRENT, startup duration); unlisted things (pages, sources, findings); typed-sheet verbs; the exam marks READ's turn without the BIND follow-up; FRAME is still not built.
release_note: The exam now asks the way the desk does. Reading your words on Home Demo is now asked: the desk's list is read once together with the reading brief, when a model is ready or when the desk changes, so each question reads only your request. The next-step pick goes through the order test, and a planted pick that the test catches is no longer counted as harm. Asking you a question is never counted as harm. Page reading is judged by precision and recall: 2 to 4 right marks are right. The 4B model's own vocabulary is read again for exact token counts. A list of the exam items that disagree with the build is kept for the test pass. On a stand-in worker the short exam asks 114 of its 127 questions. Not tested.
